title: Basic workflow
text: Biologists working regulatory agencies like United States Department Agriculture Canadian Food Inspection Agency often need quickly estimate potential geographic distribution plant species performing formal pest risk analysis. protoclim package designed help biologists perform task estimating plant species’ potential geographic distribution basis species’ known distribution climatically similar areas elsewhere world (.e. climate matching).

title: Basic workflow
text: provide overview basic protoclim workflow, use following example datasets: bryonia_alba, GBIF occurrence data Bryonia alba, eastern white-bryony climate_layers_ssp370_2011_2040(), downscaled Köppen-Geiger classes, plant hardiness zones, precipitation bands present day (2011-2040) climate SSP3-7.0 high emission scenario. get familiar data, let’s look rows occurrence data Bryonia alba Now let’s look output climate_layers_ssp370_2011_2040(), SpatRaster object three layers: one Köppen-Geiger climate classes, one precipitation bands, one plant hardiness zones. layer actually average, mode, taken across multiple global climate models. See protoclimData repository GitHub additional details. proceeding rest workflow, recommend spending time cleaning occurrence data bryonia_alba. Cleaning occurrence data nuanced often labour-intensive process requires good understanding plant species’ biology. , perform automated cleaning using CoordinateCleaner package. recommend reading Cleaning GBIF data use biogeography CoordinateCleaner authors additional information cleaning occurrence data.
code: head(bryonia_alba) #> # A tibble: 6 x 9 #>   datasetName basisOfRecord species countryCode decimalLatitude decimalLongitude #>   <chr>       <chr>         <chr>   <chr>                 <dbl>            <dbl> #> 1 Artportalen HUMAN_OBSERV~ Bryoni~ SE                     59.3             18.1 #> 2 Artportalen HUMAN_OBSERV~ Bryoni~ SE                     59.0             18.3 #> 3 Artportalen HUMAN_OBSERV~ Bryoni~ SE                     57.2             12.2 #> 4 Artportalen HUMAN_OBSERV~ Bryoni~ SE                     57.2             12.2 #> 5 Artportalen HUMAN_OBSERV~ Bryoni~ SE                     57.1             12.4 #> # i 1 more row #> # i 3 more variables: habitat <chr>, locality <chr>, year <int> climate_layers_ssp370_2011_2040() #> class       : SpatRaster #> size        : 2088, 4320, 3  (nrow, ncol, nlyr) #> resolution  : 0.08333333, 0.08333333  (x, y) #> extent      : -180.0001, 179.9999, -90.00014, 83.99986  (xmin, xmax, ymin, ymax) #> coord. ref. : lon/lat WGS 84 (EPSG:4326) #> source      : climate_layers_ssp370_2011_2040.tif #> colors rgb  : 1, 2, 3 #> names       : kgc_mode, pb_mode, phz_mode #> min values  :        1,       1,        1 #> max values  :       30,      11,       28 # Remove all occurrence records without coordinates bryonia_alba <- dplyr::filter_out(   bryonia_alba,   is.na(decimalLatitude),   is.na(decimalLongitude) )  # Convert ISO 2 country codes to ISO 3 country codes for use with CoordinateCleaner bryonia_alba <- dplyr::mutate(   bryonia_alba,   countryCode = countrycode::countrycode(     countryCode,     origin = 'iso2c',     destination = 'iso3c'   ) )  # Keep only clean occurrence data using CoordinateCleaner bryonia_alba <- CoordinateCleaner::clean_coordinates(   bryonia_alba,   value = "clean" )

title: Basic workflow
text: first step protoclim climate matching workflow classify suitability level three climate layers climate_layers_ssp370_2011_2040(). essence, process involves combining occurrence data bryonia_alba climate variable climate_layers_ssp370_2011_2040(), counting number occurrence records level climate variable, calculating proportion occurrence records within level climate variable. proportion occurrence records within level climate variable informs suitability classifications based following cutoffs: process performed classify_levels() function, takes input SpatRaster object climate layers tibble occurrence data. output list tibbles, one per climate layer, suitability classification level climate layer. shown output, classified suitability level climate variable Bryonia alba based known distribution Bryonia alba proportional occurrence level. example, Bryonia alba never occurred Köppen-Geiger climate classes 1 4 levels therefore classified suitable. next step feed suitability classifications back global raster climate data cell within raster can assigned suitability classification based climate variable. suitability classifications Köppen-Geiger classes, plant hardiness zones, precipitation bands, likely differ variables measure different aspects climate. Therefore, take minimum suitability classification across three climate variables assign overall suitability classification cell raster. process performed classify_cells() function, takes input SpatRaster object climate layers list tibbles suitability classifications level climate layer. output SpatRaster object original climate variables relabelled suitability well additional layer containing overall suitability classification cell raster. point, global raster climate data cell classified overall suitability Bryonia alba. final step visualize results. can tailor visualization particular pest risk area use whichever supported visualization library prefer. , crop raster extent Canada Canada continental United States, repropject raster appropriate projection, plot climate suitability map.

i 23 more rows cell_suitability <- classify_cells(   climate_layers_ssp370_2011_2040(),   level_suitability )  cell_suitability #> class       : SpatRaster #> size        : 2088, 4320, 4  (nrow, ncol, nlyr) #> resolution  : 0.08333333, 0.08333333  (x, y) #> extent      : -180.0001, 179.9999, -90.00014, 83.99986  (xmin, xmax, ymin, ymax) #> coord. ref. : lon/lat WGS 84 (EPSG:4326) #> source(s)   : memory #> varnames    : climate_layers_ssp370_2011_2040 #>               climate_layers_ssp370_2011_2040 #>               climate_layers_ssp370_2011_2040 #>                #> names       :     kgc_mode,      pb_mode,     phz_mode,      overall #> min values  : Not suitable, Not suitable, Not suitable, Not suitable #> max values  :     Suitable,     Suitable,     Suitable,     Suitable pra <-   rnaturalearth::ne_states(country = c("Canada", "United States of America")) |>   dplyr::filter_out(name == "Hawaii") |>   terra::vect()  cell_suitability[["overall"]] |>   terra::crop(pra, mask = TRUE) |>   terra::project("EPSG:3347", method = "near", progress = FALSE) |>   terra::trim() |>   terra::plot(axes = FALSE)

title: Climate Matching to Estimate Geographic Distributions of Plants
text: protoclim R package estimating plant species’ potential geographic distribution basis species’ known distribution climatically similar areas elsewhere world (.e. climate matching). protoclim package designed used biologists regulatory agencies perform formal pest risk analysis. end, protoclim package designed quickly easily produce mappable estimates plants species’ potential geographic distribution. Inspiration protoclim drawn heavily Proto3, GIS workflow developed used United States Department Agriculture weed risk assessment process. per Proto3, protoclim estimates plant species’ geographic distribution based global occurrence level following categorical climate classification systems. Köppen-Geiger classes Plant hardiness zones Precipitation bands Multiple high-resolution global rasters containing climate variables available download Zenodo. present, rasters available combination time periods (present vs. future) emission scenarios (high vs. -high). details, please see associated repository protoclimData. Besides raster climate data, data required use protoclim species occurrence data Global Biodiversity Information Facility (GBIF). Users encouraged download climate rasters Zenodo occurrence data focal species GBIF. demonstration purposes, protoclim comes two example datasets: bryonia_alba, GBIF occurrence data Bryonia alba, eastern white-bryony climate_layers_ssp370_2011_2040(), downscaled Köppen-Geiger classes, plant hardiness zones, precipitation bands present day (2011-2040) climate SSP3-7.0 high emission scenario.
